news.headline: The BayNet: Maryland Zoo Now Offers Free Vision Assistance App For Guests
ReBokeh Goes Global: Leading Low-Vision Tech Now Available on Android
KPNX: Phoenix Sky Harbor partners with company to help low-vision travelers

paragraphs: ReBokeh Vision Technologies sells a mobile app for people with low vision, built to use the sight they have rather than to route around it. The app runs on the camera of a device the user already owns and enables adjustments to contrast, brightness, colors and inversion filters. The about page traces the company to a founder who was offered audio only tools despite having significant residual vision.

The app is offered in two forms, ReBokeh for Organizations and ReBokeh for Individuals. ReBokeh All-Access uses geofencing technology to unlock the full set of features for anyone in a partner space, on their own personal device.

The home page carries testimonials naming MIA, the Houston Museum of Natural Science and the Art Museum of South Texas. A quote from the Miami-Dade County Mayor says that MIA is the first airport in the world to provide the app to travelers with vision challenges.

quote.text: Re-Bokeh is re-clarifying of what is out of focus.
